title: The entropy conjecture for C¹ maps
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's theorem (2026) that Shub's entropy conjecture fails for continuously differentiable maps: a noninvertible C^1 self-map of a compact manifold of dimension 2q+3 >= 7 has topological entropy zero while its action on second real homology has the eigenvalue 2. The first lesson defines topological entropy by separated sets, proves that pointwise attraction to a compact invariant set of zero entropy forces zero entropy, and proves that radial register maps have zero entropy. The second builds the map: a clock on a circle, a main sphere coordinate that squares, and register spheres that receive predicted phases weighted by L^(1-m); it proves that the map is C^1. The third proves that every orbit tends to the set where the clock stops at 50 or to the set where the main coordinate is infinite and the registers vanish. The fourth proves zero entropy and shows that the class of a sphere is an eigenvector with eigenvalue 2, because squaring has degree two on the Riemann sphere.
prerequisites: core courses Real Analysis I and II (C10, C20): Lebl, Basic Analysis I-II, Definition 7.4.7, Theorems 6.2.10, 7.5.6, 7.5.11, 8.3.7, Proposition 8.4.6
core course Algebraic Topology (D60): Fomberg, Algebraic Topology, Proposition 1.9, Theorems 1.13 and 1.23, Definition 1.27, Remark 1.35
Local tools for bundles and transport (DG-FND), Theorem 3.1 (cutoff functions)
Orientations and fundamental classes (poincare-duality-on-manifolds), Section 1, Proposition 3.2, Lemma 3.4, Corollary 3.5, Theorem 4.1, Corollary 5.1

Differences: the eigenvalue is proved with the explicit eigenvector i_*[Sigma] from f(0,z,0) = (1,z^2,0) (no finite dimensionality of H_2(M;R) is needed); deg(z^2) = 2 is proved with real coefficients from the complex orientation and the local degree of the orientation lesson; the attraction proof treats simultaneous readouts and the case z = infinity explicitly; non-surjectivity is added; the cover condition (3.1) needs at least two windows, so q >= 2 and dim M >= 7 (the preprint's list of choices allows q >= 1, which (3.1) excludes; its theorem asserts only that some q works, and the Lean proof uses q = 3). Fomberg's notes (exact free edition, PDF sha256 148aba71473e3201993e562c5e5d0f05f1a0417f4bcbd4593bead5ab236e43cd) read for the cited statements.

open_obligations: Finite dimensionality of H_k(M;R) for a compact manifold M. Stated in Section 2 of the first lesson to identify rho(f_*) with the spectral radius on total homology; not used in any proof (the course only uses that a real eigenvector with eigenvalue 2 gives rho(f_*) >= 2). Intended home: a lesson on the finiteness of the homology of compact manifolds in the Poincare duality course.

Context only, not used in any proof: Manning's theorem (first homology), Misiurewicz-Przytycki (degree), Yomdin (C^infinity maps), Saghin-Xia and Liao-Viana-Yang (classes of C^1 diffeomorphisms), named in Section 2 of the first lesson and Remark 5.3 of the fourth; the variational principle in Remark 3.2 of the first lesson; the diffeomorphism of M with S^1 x (S^2)^(q+1) in Section 5 of the fourth lesson.
